subject: Islamic Studies
q: Property that comes to the Islamic state from enemies without fighting is called:
explanation: Surah Al-Hashr describes Fay, such as the lands of Banu Nadir, which went to the state for public benefit rather than to the soldiers.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Withholding goods from the market to raise their prices is called:
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said that only a sinner hoards (Muslim); Ihtikar harms the public by creating artificial scarcity.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an calls the spendthrifts (mubadhdhirin):
explanation: Surah Al-Isra condemns squandering (tabdhir), saying the wasteful are brothers of the devils.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In the Islamic economic system, the real owner of all wealth is:
o: Allah, with man as a trustee
explanation: Man holds wealth as a trust (amanah) and must earn and spend it within the limits set by Allah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Surah Al-Mutaffifin condemns those who:
explanation: It warns those who take full measure from others but give less when they measure or weigh for them.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The transfer of a debt from one debtor to another is called:
explanation: In Hawalah the creditor agrees to recover the debt from a third party; the Prophet (PBUH) told creditors to accept such a transfer to a solvent person.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A contract of guarantee or suretyship is called:
explanation: In Kafalah a guarantor takes responsibility for another’s obligation if he fails to fulfil it.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: An asset given as security for a debt is called:
explanation: The Qur’an mentions a pledge taken in hand when no scribe is found; the Prophet (PBUH) pledged his armour for food.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Property entrusted to another person for safekeeping is called:
explanation: Wadi‘ah is a trust: the keeper must return it and is liable only for negligence; Ariyah is lending an item for use.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: An agreement in which a landowner gives land to a cultivator for a share of the produce is called:
explanation: Muzara‘ah is sharecropping of land; Musaqah is a similar arrangement for orchards in return for a share of the fruit.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Diminishing Musharakah, used in Islamic home financing, is a partnership in which:
o: The customer gradually buys the bank’s share of the asset
The bank’s share increases over time
The asset is never transferred to the customer
explanation: The customer pays rent for the bank’s share while buying it in instalments until he becomes the sole owner.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The minimum number of sheep or goats on which Zakat becomes due is:
explanation: According to the Prophet’s (PBUH) instructions, one goat is due on every 40 to 120 freely grazing sheep or goats; 5 is the minimum for camels.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which best describes the economic effect of Zakat?
o: It transfers wealth to the needy and discourages hoarding
It increases the wealth of the rich
It replaces all other forms of income
explanation: Since idle savings diminish by Zakat each year, owners are encouraged to invest, while the poor receive a share of wealth.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Islamic banking seeks to replace interest mainly with:
explanation: Instead of a fixed return on money, Islamic banks use Mudarabah, Musharakah, Murabahah, Ijarah and similar contracts.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: When asked to fix prices in Madinah during a rise in prices, the Holy Prophet (PBUH):
o: Fixed the prices of all goods
Declined, saying Allah is the One who sets prices
Ordered the traders to leave the market
explanation: In a Hadith (Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi) he declined and said he wished to meet Allah without having wronged anyone, favouring free and fair markets.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Spending one’s wealth in the way of Allah is called:
explanation: The Qur’an repeatedly urges Infaq fi sabilillah; Israf is extravagance and Iktinaz is hoarding gold and silver.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’anic warning against those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in Allah’s way appears in Surah:
explanation: Surah At-Tawbah warns that hoarded gold and silver will be heated in the Fire and used to brand those who hoarded it.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A sale in which the goods are delivered at once but the price is paid at a later agreed date is called:
explanation: Bai‘ Mu’ajjal defers the price; in Salam it is the goods that are deferred while the price is paid in advance.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Charity whose reward continues after death, such as a well, a school or a mosque, is called:
explanation: Sahih Muslim reports that a person’s deeds end at death except continuing charity, beneficial knowledge and a righteous child who prays for him.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: What is the name of the constitutional body that advises Parliament and the Provincial Assemblies on whether laws conform to the injunctions of Islam?
explanation: The Council of Islamic Ideology is a constitutional advisory body; it recommends measures to bring laws into conformity with the Qur’an and Sunnah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Council of Islamic Ideology was first created, as the Advisory Council of Islamic Ideology, under the Constitution of:
explanation: The 1962 Constitution set up an Advisory Council of Islamic Ideology; the 1973 Constitution renamed it the Council of Islamic Ideology.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Federal Shariat Court of Pakistan was established in:
explanation: The Federal Shariat Court was created in 1980 through a constitutional amendment by President Zia-ul-Haq.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The main function of the Federal Shariat Court of Pakistan is to:
o: Issue religious edicts on personal matters
Announce the sighting of the moon
Examine whether laws are repugnant to the injunctions of Islam
explanation: The Court may examine any law and declare it void to the extent it is repugnant to the Qur’an and Sunnah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Appeals against decisions of the Federal Shariat Court are heard by the:
o: Shariat Appellate Bench of the Supreme Court
explanation: The Shariat Appellate Bench of the Supreme Court, including Ulema judges, hears appeals from the Federal Shariat Court.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Objectives Resolution (1949) declared that sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to:
explanation: The Resolution stated that sovereignty belongs to Allah and that authority is exercised by the people as a sacred trust within limits prescribed by Him.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Pakistan was first named the ‘Islamic Republic of Pakistan’ in the Constitution of:
explanation: The 1956 Constitution adopted the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan; the 1962 Constitution first dropped “Islamic” and it was restored in 1963.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, under which Zakat began to be deducted from bank accounts in Pakistan, was promulgated in:
explanation: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance of 1980 introduced state collection and distribution of Zakat through Zakat committees.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Hudood Ordinances were promulgated in 1979 during the rule of:
explanation: The Hudood Ordinances were part of Zia-ul-Haq’s Islamisation programme and introduced Hadd punishments into Pakistani law.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Protection of Women (Criminal Laws Amendment) Act, 2006 mainly amended the:
explanation: The 2006 Act moved rape from the Hudood law to the Pakistan Penal Code and changed the procedure for Zina cases.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Muslim Family Laws Ordinance was promulgated in 1961 during the government of:
explanation: The Ordinance followed the report of the Rashid Commission on marriage and family laws and was issued by Ayub Khan’s government.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, a husband wishing to contract another marriage must obtain permission from the:
explanation: The Ordinance requires written permission of the Arbitration Council, headed by the Union Council chairman, for a subsequent marriage.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Pakistan, the official body that announces the sighting of the new moon for Islamic months is the:
explanation: The Central Ruet-e-Hilal Committee announces the beginning of Ramadan, Shawwal and other Islamic months.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation was founded in 1969 in response to:
o: The arson attack on Masjid al-Aqsa
explanation: After the fire at Al-Aqsa in August 1969, Muslim leaders met in Rabat in September 1969 and founded the organisation.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The headquarters of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) is in:
explanation: The OIC General Secretariat is based in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, pending its planned move to Al-Quds.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The second Islamic Summit Conference of the OIC was held in 1974 at:
explanation: The Lahore Summit of February 1974, hosted by Pakistan, brought together leaders of the Muslim world and strengthened the OIC.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) is headquartered in:
explanation: The IsDB, an OIC-linked multilateral bank that began operations in 1975, is based in Jeddah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Muslim World League (Rabitat al-Alam al-Islami), founded in 1962, is headquartered in:
explanation: The Muslim World League, a non-governmental Islamic organisation, was established in Makkah in 1962.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The book ‘Orientalism’ (1978), a critique of Western representations of the Muslim East, was written by:
explanation: Edward Said argued that Western scholarship often portrayed the East through stereotypes that served colonial power.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The ‘Clash of Civilizations’ thesis was put forward by:
explanation: Huntington argued in the 1990s that future conflicts would arise along cultural and religious lines, a view widely criticised.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The UN General Assembly has designated which day as the International Day to Combat Islamophobia?
explanation: A 2022 UN resolution, introduced by Pakistan on behalf of the OIC, designated 15 March, the date of the Christchurch mosque attacks.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an forbids ‘Ghuluw’ in religion, which means:
explanation: The Qur’an and Hadith warn against exceeding the limits in religion, noting that earlier nations were destroyed by extremism.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Declaring another Muslim to be a disbeliever is called:
explanation: Takfir was the hallmark of the Khawarij; the Prophet (PBUH) warned that calling a Muslim a kafir returns upon the accuser if untrue.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘Paigham-e-Pakistan’ (2018) is:
o: A five-year plan for Islamic banking
A declaration by Pakistani religious scholars against terrorism and suicide attacks
explanation: Endorsed by more than 1,800 scholars of all schools, it declared suicide bombing and armed rebellion against the state to be forbidden.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Amman Message (2004) is known for:
o: Recognising the major schools of Islamic law and restricting Takfir
explanation: Issued in Jordan and endorsed by hundreds of scholars, it affirmed the validity of the major Sunni, Shia and Ibadi schools and forbade declaring their followers apostates.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘A Common Word Between Us and You’ (2007) was:
o: An open letter from Muslim scholars to Christian leaders on love of God and neighbour
explanation: Muslim scholars invited Christian leaders to common ground on the love of God and love of neighbour, drawing on a Qur’anic phrase.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’anic call ‘Come to a word common between us and you’ is addressed to:
explanation: Surah Aal-e-Imran invites Jews and Christians to the common ground of worshipping Allah alone, a basis for interfaith dialogue.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Pan-Islamism in the nineteenth century is most closely associated with:
explanation: Afghani called for the unity of the Muslim world against Western colonialism and for intellectual revival.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In ‘The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam’, Allama Iqbal described Ijtihad as:
o: A closed door since the classical age
A duty of the ruler alone
The principle of movement in the structure of Islam
explanation: In his sixth lecture Iqbal called Ijtihad the principle of movement and urged its revival for modern needs.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Allama Iqbal proposed that in modern times Ijtihad could be exercised collectively through:
explanation: Iqbal suggested transferring the power of Ijtihad to an elected Muslim assembly, advised by scholars, as a form of Ijma.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Mit Ghamr savings bank (1963), an early modern experiment in interest-free banking, was set up in:
explanation: Ahmad al-Najjar founded the Mit Ghamr savings bank in Egypt’s Nile Delta on profit-sharing principles.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Dubai Islamic Bank, often described as the first modern commercial Islamic bank, was established in:
explanation: Dubai Islamic Bank began in 1975, the same year the Islamic Development Bank started operations.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: AAOIFI, which issues Shariah and accounting standards for Islamic financial institutions, is based in:
explanation: The Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial Institutions is headquartered in Manama, Bahrain.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Islamic view of Din as a complete code of life contrasts most directly with:
explanation: Secularism confines religion to private life, whereas Islam gives guidance for public, economic and political affairs as well.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The International Islamic Fiqh Academy, a forum for collective Ijtihad on modern issues, works under the:
explanation: Created by the OIC and based in Jeddah, the Academy brings jurists together to issue collective resolutions on contemporary questions.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In its basic sense, ‘Jihad’ means:
o: Striving in the way of Allah
explanation: Jihad comes from juhd (effort) and includes struggle against one’s self, with knowledge and wealth; armed Jihad is only under lawful authority and rules.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Charter of Makkah (2019), endorsed by scholars under the Muslim World League, mainly emphasises:
o: Peaceful coexistence and rejection of extremism
explanation: Adopted in May 2019, it called for tolerance, the rights of religious diversity and rejection of hate and violence.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 replaced the Evidence Act of 1872 in order to:
o: Bring the law of evidence into line with Islamic injunctions
Regulate the sighting of the moon
explanation: Promulgated under Zia-ul-Haq, the Order reshaped the rules of evidence, including the competence of witnesses, in the light of Islamic law.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In 1991 the Federal Shariat Court of Pakistan declared that bank interest:
o: Falls within Riba and is repugnant to Islam
Is permissible as a service charge
Is a matter outside its jurisdiction
Is lawful for government loans only
explanation: In November 1991 the Court held that interest in all its forms is Riba; the case later went to the Shariat Appellate Bench and back to the FSC.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Enforcement of Shari‘ah Act, 1991 was passed during the government of:
explanation: The Act, passed in Nawaz Sharif’s first government, declared the Qur’an and Sunnah the supreme law of Pakistan within the constitutional framework.
